title: Bright Field Imaging of Swarming Behavior in C. elegans
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vyhe7t6
materials: Images are segmented in real time by the Gecko software.

steps.title: Prepare imaging plates
steps.instruction: Pour and store imaging plates with low‑peptone NGM agar.

substeps.instruction: Pour 3.5 mL low‑peptone NGM agar (0.013% Difco Bacto, 2% Bio/Agar, BioGene) into each 35 mm Petri dish exactly seven days before imaging.
Store the poured plates at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Seed plate center with OP50
steps.instruction: Add OP50 spot and incubate overnight.

substeps.instruction: Spot 75 µL cold diluted OP50 (OD = 0.38) onto the center of each imaging plate.
Incubate plates overnight at room temperature; use the next day.

steps.title: Bleach‑synchronize worms
steps.instruction: Synchronize gravid hermaphrodites by bleach and keep on rotator.

substeps.instruction: Bleach‑synchronize gravid hermaphrodites.
Place synchronized worms on a rotator at 20 °C and keep until needed.

steps.title: Re‑feed starved L1s
steps.instruction: Transfer starved L1 larvae onto culture plates and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, transfer starved L1 worms onto 3–4 culture plates.
Culture plates: 55 mm Petri dishes with 15 mL low‑peptone NGM agar (0.013% Difco Bacto, 2% Bio/Agar) seeded with OP50.
Incubate the plates at 20 °C.

steps.title: Wash worms from culture plates
steps.instruction: Wash harvested worms with M9 and concentrate them.

substeps.instruction: Wash worms off the culture plates with M9 buffer.
Collect the wash in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Perform two additional washes with M9.
After the final wash, aspirate as much supernatant as possible.

steps.title: Transfer worms to imaging plate
steps.instruction: Place forty worms in an M9 drop on the imaging plate away from bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, transfer exactly forty worms onto the imaging plate.
Place worms in a small M9 drop away from the bacterial lawn.

steps.title: Acquire time‑lapse imaging
steps.instruction: Record 20‑hour bright‑field movies at 25 Hz with red illumination.

substeps.instruction: Start imaging immediately after transfer while worms remain in the liquid drop.
Record on the Phoenix six‑camera rig (Dalsa Genie G2‑GM10‑T2041) for 20 h with 630 nm red LED illumination (CCS Inc.) at 25 Hz using Gecko software v2.0.3.1.
Maintain the imaging plate at 20 °C throughout the recording.

steps.title: Trim recordings to swarming phase
steps.instruction: Manually truncate movies to keep only aggregation and swarming dynamics.

substeps.instruction: Manually truncate each recording to retain only the aggregation and swarming phases.
Define the start time as the moment the liquid dries and worms exit the initial drop.
Define the end time as when food is depleted and worms disperse with increased crawling speed.
